Passage VII
Distillation is a method for separating compounds
based on their boiling points (BPs). Figure 1 shows a
distillation apparatus consisting of a distilling flask (DF),
a distilling column (DC), a distilling head (DH), a
thermometer, a condenser, and a collection flask (CF).
The DF contains a 1:1 ethanol/H
O mixture by volume.
Ethanol has a BP of 78.4°C and H
O has a BP of 100.0°C
at 1 atmosphere (atm). Each of 4 students (Students 1
gave their opinions on how the distillation would proceed
when the mixture was heated.
Figure 1

DF

mixture
Student 1
Ethanol and H
O are far apart in BP, so they can be
separated by distillation. The mixture will boil at 78.4°C,
the BP of ethanol. The vapor will be pure ethanol at
78.4°C, which will condense and collect in the CF. When
all the ethanol has distilled, the liquid remaining in the DF
will boil at 100°C. The vapor will be pure H
O at 100°C,
and will condense and collect in the CF.
Student 2
Student 1 is incorrect. Ethanol and H
O are too close
in BP to be separated by distillation. The mixture will boil
at 89.2°C, halfway between the BPs of the ethanol and
H
O. The vapor will have the same composition as the
mixture and will be at 89.2°C. It will condense into the
same ethanol/H
O mixture and collect in the CF.
Student 3
Ethanol and H
O are close in BP but can be separated
by distillation. The mixture will boil at 81.7°C. Ethanol
has a lower BP than H
O, so the vapor will contain more
ethanol than water. This vapor will condense and
revaporize many times as it moves up the DC, becoming
enriched in ethanol. The vapor that reaches the condenser
first will be 100% ethanol at 78.4°C, and will condense
and collect in the CF. As more of the mixture in the DF
vaporizes, the amount of H
O in the vapor will increase
and so will the proportion of H
O in the liquid that collects
in the CF.
Student 4
Student 3 is correct except ethanol and H
O can only
be partially separated by distillation. The vapor that
reaches the condenser first and collects in the CF will be
96% ethanol and 4% H
O, the ethanol/H
O azeotrope (a
mixture of 2 liquids that boils at a lower temperature than
either liquid alone), at 78.1°C.
